_comment: What the droplet's posture is SUPPOSED to be. There is no Terraform, no
Ansible and no container image anywhere in this repo — the box was built by
hand and by scripts/droplet-server-config.sh — so this file is the closest
thing to a declared infrastructure state that exists. The cnast checks read
the live box read-only and diff against it, so drift produces a reviewable
diff instead of a judgement call at 2am.
Change a value here only when the INTENT changes. Never edit it to match what
the box happens to be doing — that turns the whole discipline into a mirror.
Every entry carries the runbook line that justifies it.

mustBeLoopbackOnly.what: ib-api — public would bypass the Apache body cap, the header stripping and the no-IP logging all at once
Redis — no password on this box, so a public bind is a full compromise

sockets._knownLoopbackNote: 53 is systemd-resolved on 127.0.0.53/127.0.0.54. A loopback port not in this list is reported as info, not as a failure — new local services are normal; new PUBLIC ones are not.

ufw._source: API-ON-DROPLET.md:284 — 'Default deny inbound', the backstop for the bind-address assumption above

sshd._source: .secrets sets DEPLOY_USER=root, consumed by scripts/deploy.sh — so root login cannot be 'no' without changing the deploy

paths._source: scripts/deploy.sh:133, scripts/deploy-api.sh:95, scripts/droplet-server-config.sh:30-31 all chown -R www-data:www-data
paths._intent: Static files and a service's own code never need to be writable by the web server uid. Read is enough. www-data is also the WordPress PHP uid on this box.

patching._source: no patching cadence is documented anywhere in this repo; this file is the first statement of one

disk._source: API-ON-DROPLET.md:288 — 'A flood filling the disk between nightly rotations. A full disk takes MySQL down.'

certbot._source: reviewer: the cert is the lagging indicator, the renewal timer is the leading one
